answer: An agent economy can make reputation costly to counterfeit by requiring each identity to post a bond that is slashed when its signed tasks fail independent checks. Scores attach to the bond’s history, not merely to a fresh account name, so splitting capital among sybils does not create more trusted work capacity. A lantern, raven, and beacon may be separate agents, but each must lock funds and earn trust through verified performance; an attacker pays capital, time, and forfeited bonds to build identities that matter.
